Subtitle: Satellite Intelligence for Future Lunar and Martian Exploration
-----------------
Project Summary
Developed by MOROCCO FIFA WORLD CUP 2030
Lunar & Mars Analogs Explorer is a geospatial research project designed to identify and characterize terrestrial environments that could help prepare for future permanent lunar bases and Mars exploration missions.

Using open Earth observation data from NASA and other space agencies, our project aims to compare Earth's landscapes with selected lunar and Martian regions based on topography, geology, surface conditions, temperature, water and ice indicators, dust processes, and operational suitability.

The proposed platform combines satellite intelligence, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and similarity-ranking methods to discover potentially underexplored terrestrial analog sites worldwide.

Through interactive mapping and comparative visualizations, users will be able to explore promising locations, understand their planetary similarities, and identify important environmental differences and scientific limitations.

Our goal is to transform Earth observation data into practical scientific insights that support mission preparation, technology testing, and safer future space exploration.

What does it do or how does it work?It is a geospatial research platform designed to identify and characterize terrestrial environments capable of serving as analog laboratories for future permanent lunar bases and Mars exploration missions.
Lunar_Mars_Analogs_Explorer_Demo.pptxIt operates via a 4-step workflow: Collection of Earth observation and planetary data; Comparison of topography, geology, temperatures, and resources; Evaluation (mission-specific similarity scoring with confidence levels); and Interactive exploration of candidate sites and their environmental limitations.
Lunar_Mars_Analogs_Explorer_Demo.pptxIt also integrates Python-based machine learning models (analyzing crop adaptation to CO₂) and JavaScript 2D games (using Phaser) leveraging real-time NASA data APIs.
PHOTO_DAWGUILY_TAREQ.jpegWhat benefits does it have?It replaces simple subjective visual resemblances with rigorous, evidence-based comparisons.
Lunar_Mars_Analogs_Explorer_Demo.pptxIt provides researchers and space agencies with transparent evaluations of terrestrial analogs (such as the case studies in Morocco: Erg Chebbi, Jbel Saghro, and Agafay) to test instruments, navigation systems, and mission strategies.
Lunar_Mars_Analogs_Explorer_Demo.pptx+ 1What is the intended impact of the project?To transform raw Earth observation and planetary data into practical scientific insights to support mission preparation, technological testing, and safer future space exploration.To make planetary data and analog comparisons more accessible for scientific studies and engineering trials.Lunar_Mars_Analogs_Explorer_Demo.pptxWhat tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?Programming Languages: Python (for ML models) and JavaScript with Phaser (for 2D game development).
PHOTO_DAWGUILY_TAREQ.jpegDesign & Graphics: Piskel (for creating and editing pixel art sprites and images).
PHOTO_DAWGUILY_TAREQ.jpegNASA Data & APIs: NASA Earth Observatory, NASA Harvest, Landsat imagery (historical comparisons since 1984), NDVI APIs, data pathfinders (Extreme Heat, Floods, Water Management), U.S. Drought Monitor, NTRS, as well as topographic data from LRO/LOLA and MOLA/HiRISE.
Lunar_Mars_Analogs_Explorer_Demo.pptx+ 1Software & GIS: Google Earth Engine, Google Colab, QGIS, Streamlit, and Leaflet.
Lunar_Mars_Analogs_Explorer_Demo.pptx+ 1How is your project creative?It bridges cutting-edge aerospace research with interactive, gamified education by combining rigorous geospatial analysis with 2D web gaming and pixel art.Instead of treating Earth as a uniform copy of another world, it isolates specific planetary features (lunar base constraints on one side, rover mobility and Martian dust dynamics on the other) to distinctly evaluate each mission type.
Lunar_Mars_Analogs_Explorer_Demo.pptxWhat factors did your team consider?Mission-Specific Priorities: Distinguishing evaluation criteria for a lunar base (polar illumination, slope, thermal environment, water-ice indicators) from those for Mars exploration (geological alteration, dunes, dust transport, past hydrological processes).
Lunar_Mars_Analogs_Explorer_Demo.pptxData Limitations & Transparency: Acknowledging crucial limitations—such as Earth's inability to reproduce lunar gravity/vacuum or Mars' thin atmosphere and radiation—while explicitly incorporating data confidence and missing data management into similarity scores.
